blocks.text: The wish

content.value: A large benchmarking test utilizing Scaffy to the max — documenting the usefulness of Scaffy and Barkpark, with a great flagship Paper as the deliverable. Real research: all use cases, potential leaps to ascend Scaffy into a token-sparing consistency speed machine, auto-detection of patterns, one clear understanding of what Scaffy IS. And the honesty law, in the user's own words: no bloat — we do not want to use it unless it actually performs A LOT better. A benchmark that only flatters is worthless.

This is W6 of the Scaffy epic: a MEASUREMENT wave. W1–W4 are sealed (7-command corpus, validate/fmt/run/remove/pull/ls --remote, commands served from guerrilla, reversibility matrix 6/6). W5 (catalog 7→14, ONEOF) is completing concurrently — rounds 2–3 in flight, PR #3917 healing the corpus count. W6 does not extend the catalog; it weighs it.

blocks.text: Direction (tentative — Decide finalizes after two exploration rounds)

content.value: The finished experience is TWO papers and a verdict. First, a short pre-registration paper (the optical-duels-prereg discipline: arms, chores, metrics, rep counts, and success thresholds committed BEFORE any duel runs — so the results cannot be quietly re-scoped to flatter). Second, THE flagship Paper: premium native blocks telling the whole story — one clear definition of what Scaffy is, the use-case atlas with frequency×pain evidence, the measured duel numbers, the honest boundary where Scaffy loses with a quantified crossover, and the leaps ranked with build-cost estimates. The verdict the Paper must be able to deliver honestly: 'use Scaffy for THESE shapes because it is measurably ~Nx cheaper/faster/more consistent; do NOT use it for THOSE, here is where the line sits.'

Duel design I lean toward (lean, pre-registered, small chores preferred for repetition): 3 catalog chores × 3 arms × up to 3 reps, plus one BOUNDARY CONTROL chore Scaffy should lose. Chores: add-error-shape (the frequency champion — 38 real clause-adds in errors.ex history), add-cli-verb (smallest, zero-Go, cheapest to repeat), add-oban-worker (REANCHOR accretion — run it TWICE per rep to measure the accretion case). Boundary control: a real, recent one-off edit no catalog command expresses — the arm-inversion that keeps the benchmark honest. The flagship add-block-type is the showpiece, not the workhorse: 1 rep, arm A vs arm C only (arm B at ~56–80k tokens × 3 surfaces × reps would blow the budget for a number W1 already gave us).

Arms: A = agent armed with bp scaffy run + the catalog, instructed catalog-first. B = bare agent hand-editing (the status quo). C = raw engine, no agent — zero tokens, milliseconds; C is nearly free so it runs for every chore and every rep and anchors the consistency floor (byte-determinism). A cheap A′ sub-duel where affordable: agent with scaffy AVAILABLE but NOT instructed catalog-first — this measures the doctrine gap, which is the real token-sparing machine (leap 2). Metrics per run, all mechanical: LLM tokens consumed, wall-clock, correctness (the repo's own gates green), consistency (byte-variance across reps — sha256 of the produced diff), reversibility (remove → git diff --stat empty). Every run in an isolated worktree pinned to one green base SHA (main's go suite may be red until #3917 merges — pin deliberately, never float).

Prior data folds in as evidence, cited not re-bought: W1's hand-apply pass burned ~56–80k tokens per command per agent doing what the engine does in milliseconds at zero tokens; W1's parallel builders shipped THREE grammar dialects in one wave (the consistency counterfactual); the 6/6 reversibility matrix (/papers/scaffy-reversibility-proof); W5's frequency mining (38 errors.ex clause-adds, 295 .ex+test co-creation commits, router.ex with 739 co-change partners).

[Correction, 2026-07-17 Review: this direction paragraph predates the honesty sweep — D69 later ruled the 56–80k figure UNSOURCED (never citable as data), dropped 739 as irreproducible, and the pinned-window miner (tooling/scaffy-mine) superseded 295 with 236 strict / 304 loose co-creations. The sentence stands as the wave's starting belief, not as data.]

Leaps research (the ascension axis), each ending in a ranked verdict + build-cost estimate + filed task if ratified: (1) bp scaffy discover — spec the deterministic git-history mining pass (co-change accretion files, suffix-pair co-creations, directory fingerprints; W5 did this by hand agent-side — can it be a Go pass?), prototype if cheap; (2) agent-integration doctrine — how CLAUDE.md/skills should encode catalog-first so agents reach for the catalog instead of hand-editing (informed by the A vs A′ measurement); (3) CI/watch integration — anchors drift-checked on merge via validate --repo; (4) whatever the duels reveal. The crossover quantification is mandatory: authoring a .scaffy costs X once; it pays back at frequency × per-use savings — the atlas states, per use case, which side of the line it sits on.

Operational constraints binding this wave: W5 rounds 2–3 are completing concurrently — no build slice touches scaffy/commands/ or corpus_test.go until W5 round 3 merges (declare rounds/after honestly; the dispatcher consumes round/after natively). Duel agents are EXPENSIVE — the matrix is pre-registered BEFORE spending, and nothing outside the registered matrix runs. Benchmark runs happen in isolated worktrees, never the primary checkout (which is currently behind main and shows the 7-command corpus). New paper tags are pre-registered exact-string before publish.

content.value: 1) w5-live-state — exact merge state of W5 rounds 2–3 and PR #3917; is the served catalog 7 or 14; which files are hot; the last green base SHA to pin worktrees to. Why: the duel base and the do-not-touch set both depend on it.

3) token-accounting — the concrete mechanism to measure LLM tokens per duel run in this house (workflow harness stats, transcript files, claude CLI cost output?); where W1's 56–80k figure came from and whether the same instrument still exists. Why: tokens are the headline metric; without a trustworthy meter there is no benchmark.

4) w1-prior-evidence — dig up the primary records of the W1 hand-apply pass (task evidence, wave papers): exact token numbers per command, and the three-grammar-dialects story with cites. Why: prior data the Paper cites must be traceable to primary evidence, not memory.

5) catalog-census — every command in the current catalog (7 local, up to 14 on main): what it does, op census, gates, and a size/cost classification for duel-candidate sizing (which are small enough to repeat 3×). Why: chore selection wants the smallest chores that still represent each op family.

6) chore-gate-costs — for add-error-shape, add-cli-verb, add-oban-worker, add-block-type: the exact green gates and their measured local runtimes (mix test single-file ~2–9s warm, pnpm cold 740s, docs-anchors 70–154s…). Why: N reps × arms × gates is the wall-clock budget; the matrix must fit an afternoon.

7) frequency-evidence — where W5's mining numbers live (38 errors.ex clause-adds, 295 co-creation commits, router.ex 739 partners), the exact git commands used, and whether the pass is re-runnable/extendable. Why: the atlas's frequency column and the discover spec both stand on this method.

8) discover-prior-art — co-change mining prior art already in the repo: tooling/ (codebase-quality RELATE arc computes co-change layers), tooling/scope, any git-history analyzers. Why: bp scaffy discover should steal a proven pass, not invent one; build-cost estimate depends on what exists.

9) duel-harness — mechanics of running duel agents: how to spawn an isolated agent per arm (claude CLI? workflow?), model pinning (never Haiku; same model both arms), worktree setup/teardown, how to capture tokens+wall-clock+diff per run, cost estimate per duel cell. Why: the harness design gates everything; pre-registration must name it.

10) paper-vocab-and-wall — the premium block vocabulary with exact shapes (eyebrow/ingress/byline/stats/table/diagram/terminal/callout) from the showcase + optical payloads; the LIVE tag registry (exact-string); the publish-wall rules. Why: the flagship Paper is the deliverable; its block plan should be copy-ready at Decide.

11) boundary-census — everywhere Scaffy already lost, with evidence: D60 cuts (add-changeset, add-test-fixture, update-oban-cron, add-retriever, api-route-parity retired), deferred primitives (insert-before, value-capture, composition), D11's conditional/manual steps. Why: the boundary section of the Paper is mandatory under the honesty law.

12) authoring-cost — what it actually cost to author each .scaffy (W1/W5 slice task evidence: builder tokens, review rounds, line counts). Why: the crossover math needs the amortized numerator, not a guess.

13) validate-repo-ci — what validate --repo checks today (repocheck.go), its runtime, and the cheapest honest merge-gate integration (doc-gates.yml precedent, path triggers). Why: leap 3's build-cost estimate and whether it is a this-wave slice or a filed task.

14) novel-chore-control — find 2–3 real, recent one-off edits (from git log) that NO catalog command expresses, sized similar to the duel chores; recommend one as the boundary-control chore. Why: the control arm is what makes the benchmark falsifiable rather than a flatter-piece.

blocks.text: Direction (tentative — Decide finalizes after two exploration rounds)

content.value: The finished experience is TWO papers and a verdict. First, a short pre-registration paper (the optical-duels-prereg discipline: arms, chores, metrics, rep counts, and success thresholds committed BEFORE any duel runs — so the results cannot be quietly re-scoped to flatter). Second, THE flagship Paper: premium native blocks telling the whole story — one clear definition of what Scaffy is, the use-case atlas with frequency×pain evidence, the measured duel numbers, the honest boundary where Scaffy loses with a quantified crossover, and the leaps ranked with build-cost estimates. The verdict the Paper must be able to deliver honestly: 'use Scaffy for THESE shapes because it is measurably ~Nx cheaper/faster/more consistent; do NOT use it for THOSE, here is where the line sits.'

Duel design I lean toward (lean, pre-registered, small chores preferred for repetition): 3 catalog chores × 3 arms × up to 3 reps, plus one BOUNDARY CONTROL chore Scaffy should lose. Chores: add-error-shape (the frequency champion — 38 real clause-adds in errors.ex history), add-cli-verb (smallest, zero-Go, cheapest to repeat), add-oban-worker (REANCHOR accretion — run it TWICE per rep to measure the accretion case). Boundary control: a real, recent one-off edit no catalog command expresses — the arm-inversion that keeps the benchmark honest. The flagship add-block-type is the showpiece, not the workhorse: 1 rep, arm A vs arm C only (arm B at ~56–80k tokens × 3 surfaces × reps would blow the budget for a number W1 already gave us).

Arms: A = agent armed with bp scaffy run + the catalog, instructed catalog-first. B = bare agent hand-editing (the status quo). C = raw engine, no agent — zero tokens, milliseconds; C is nearly free so it runs for every chore and every rep and anchors the consistency floor (byte-determinism). A cheap A′ sub-duel where affordable: agent with scaffy AVAILABLE but NOT instructed catalog-first — this measures the doctrine gap, which is the real token-sparing machine (leap 2). Metrics per run, all mechanical: LLM tokens consumed, wall-clock, correctness (the repo's own gates green), consistency (byte-variance across reps — sha256 of the produced diff), reversibility (remove → git diff --stat empty). Every run in an isolated worktree pinned to one green base SHA (main's go suite may be red until #3917 merges — pin deliberately, never float).

Prior data folds in as evidence, cited not re-bought: W1's hand-apply pass burned ~56–80k tokens per command per agent doing what the engine does in milliseconds at zero tokens; W1's parallel builders shipped THREE grammar dialects in one wave (the consistency counterfactual); the 6/6 reversibility matrix (/papers/scaffy-reversibility-proof); W5's frequency mining (38 errors.ex clause-adds, 295 .ex+test co-creation commits, router.ex with 739 co-change partners).

Scaffy · Wave 6 · The Benchmark — measure it or don't ship it

Scaffy W6 — The Benchmark: duels, the use-case atlas, and the ascension leaps

WAVE COMPLETE (Review, 2026-07-17) — round 1 built and reviewed: 3 of 3 slices green (prereg paper published + tags registered; duel harness smoke-proven with review fixes; canonical miner deterministic). Rounds 2–3 (run-duels, flagship-paper) are DEFERRED BY DESIGN per D73 — dispatch after round 1 merges. Debrief at the bottom of this paper.

The wish

A large benchmarking test utilizing Scaffy to the max — documenting the usefulness of Scaffy and Barkpark, with a great flagship Paper as the deliverable. Real research: all use cases, potential leaps to ascend Scaffy into a token-sparing consistency speed machine, auto-detection of patterns, one clear understanding of what Scaffy IS. And the honesty law, in the user's own words: no bloat — we do not want to use it unless it actually performs A LOT better. A benchmark that only flatters is worthless.

This is W6 of the Scaffy epic: a MEASUREMENT wave. W1–W4 are sealed (7-command corpus, validate/fmt/run/remove/pull/ls --remote, commands served from guerrilla, reversibility matrix 6/6). W5 (catalog 7→14, ONEOF) is completing concurrently — rounds 2–3 in flight, PR #3917 healing the corpus count. W6 does not extend the catalog; it weighs it.

Direction (tentative — Decide finalizes after two exploration rounds)

The finished experience is TWO papers and a verdict. First, a short pre-registration paper (the optical-duels-prereg discipline: arms, chores, metrics, rep counts, and success thresholds committed BEFORE any duel runs — so the results cannot be quietly re-scoped to flatter). Second, THE flagship Paper: premium native blocks telling the whole story — one clear definition of what Scaffy is, the use-case atlas with frequency×pain evidence, the measured duel numbers, the honest boundary where Scaffy loses with a quantified crossover, and the leaps ranked with build-cost estimates. The verdict the Paper must be able to deliver honestly: 'use Scaffy for THESE shapes because it is measurably ~Nx cheaper/faster/more consistent; do NOT use it for THOSE, here is where the line sits.'

Duel design I lean toward (lean, pre-registered, small chores preferred for repetition): 3 catalog chores × 3 arms × up to 3 reps, plus one BOUNDARY CONTROL chore Scaffy should lose. Chores: add-error-shape (the frequency champion — 38 real clause-adds in errors.ex history), add-cli-verb (smallest, zero-Go, cheapest to repeat), add-oban-worker (REANCHOR accretion — run it TWICE per rep to measure the accretion case). Boundary control: a real, recent one-off edit no catalog command expresses — the arm-inversion that keeps the benchmark honest. The flagship add-block-type is the showpiece, not the workhorse: 1 rep, arm A vs arm C only (arm B at ~56–80k tokens × 3 surfaces × reps would blow the budget for a number W1 already gave us).

Arms: A = agent armed with bp scaffy run + the catalog, instructed catalog-first. B = bare agent hand-editing (the status quo). C = raw engine, no agent — zero tokens, milliseconds; C is nearly free so it runs for every chore and every rep and anchors the consistency floor (byte-determinism). A cheap A′ sub-duel where affordable: agent with scaffy AVAILABLE but NOT instructed catalog-first — this measures the doctrine gap, which is the real token-sparing machine (leap 2). Metrics per run, all mechanical: LLM tokens consumed, wall-clock, correctness (the repo's own gates green), consistency (byte-variance across reps — sha256 of the produced diff), reversibility (remove → git diff --stat empty). Every run in an isolated worktree pinned to one green base SHA (main's go suite may be red until #3917 merges — pin deliberately, never float).

Prior data folds in as evidence, cited not re-bought: W1's hand-apply pass burned ~56–80k tokens per command per agent doing what the engine does in milliseconds at zero tokens; W1's parallel builders shipped THREE grammar dialects in one wave (the consistency counterfactual); the 6/6 reversibility matrix (/papers/scaffy-reversibility-proof); W5's frequency mining (38 errors.ex clause-adds, 295 .ex+test co-creation commits, router.ex with 739 co-change partners). [Correction, 2026-07-17 Review: this direction paragraph predates the honesty sweep — D69 later ruled the 56–80k figure UNSOURCED (never citable as data), dropped 739 as irreproducible, and the pinned-window miner (tooling/scaffy-mine) superseded 295 with 236 strict / 304 loose co-creations. The sentence stands as the wave's starting belief, not as data.]

Leaps research (the ascension axis), each ending in a ranked verdict + build-cost estimate + filed task if ratified: (1) bp scaffy discover — spec the deterministic git-history mining pass (co-change accretion files, suffix-pair co-creations, directory fingerprints; W5 did this by hand agent-side — can it be a Go pass?), prototype if cheap; (2) agent-integration doctrine — how CLAUDE.md/skills should encode catalog-first so agents reach for the catalog instead of hand-editing (informed by the A vs A′ measurement); (3) CI/watch integration — anchors drift-checked on merge via validate --repo; (4) whatever the duels reveal. The crossover quantification is mandatory: authoring a .scaffy costs X once; it pays back at frequency × per-use savings — the atlas states, per use case, which side of the line it sits on.

Operational constraints binding this wave: W5 rounds 2–3 are completing concurrently — no build slice touches scaffy/commands/ or corpus_test.go until W5 round 3 merges (declare rounds/after honestly; the dispatcher consumes round/after natively). Duel agents are EXPENSIVE — the matrix is pre-registered BEFORE spending, and nothing outside the registered matrix runs. Benchmark runs happen in isolated worktrees, never the primary checkout (which is currently behind main and shows the 7-command corpus). New paper tags are pre-registered exact-string before publish.

Survey plan — 14 scouts, one question each

1) w5-live-state — exact merge state of W5 rounds 2–3 and PR #3917; is the served catalog 7 or 14; which files are hot; the last green base SHA to pin worktrees to. Why: the duel base and the do-not-touch set both depend on it.

2) duel-precedent — read /papers/optical-duels-prereg and /papers/optical-duels-results; extract the reusable methodology skeleton: what got pre-registered, how arms/judges/metrics were framed, what the results paper's block structure was. Why: W6 reuses that discipline wholesale.

3) token-accounting — the concrete mechanism to measure LLM tokens per duel run in this house (workflow harness stats, transcript files, claude CLI cost output?); where W1's 56–80k figure came from and whether the same instrument still exists. Why: tokens are the headline metric; without a trustworthy meter there is no benchmark.

4) w1-prior-evidence — dig up the primary records of the W1 hand-apply pass (task evidence, wave papers): exact token numbers per command, and the three-grammar-dialects story with cites. Why: prior data the Paper cites must be traceable to primary evidence, not memory.

5) catalog-census — every command in the current catalog (7 local, up to 14 on main): what it does, op census, gates, and a size/cost classification for duel-candidate sizing (which are small enough to repeat 3×). Why: chore selection wants the smallest chores that still represent each op family.

6) chore-gate-costs — for add-error-shape, add-cli-verb, add-oban-worker, add-block-type: the exact green gates and their measured local runtimes (mix test single-file ~2–9s warm, pnpm cold 740s, docs-anchors 70–154s…). Why: N reps × arms × gates is the wall-clock budget; the matrix must fit an afternoon.

7) frequency-evidence — where W5's mining numbers live (38 errors.ex clause-adds, 295 co-creation commits, router.ex 739 partners), the exact git commands used, and whether the pass is re-runnable/extendable. Why: the atlas's frequency column and the discover spec both stand on this method.

8) discover-prior-art — co-change mining prior art already in the repo: tooling/ (codebase-quality RELATE arc computes co-change layers), tooling/scope, any git-history analyzers. Why: bp scaffy discover should steal a proven pass, not invent one; build-cost estimate depends on what exists.

9) duel-harness — mechanics of running duel agents: how to spawn an isolated agent per arm (claude CLI? workflow?), model pinning (never Haiku; same model both arms), worktree setup/teardown, how to capture tokens+wall-clock+diff per run, cost estimate per duel cell. Why: the harness design gates everything; pre-registration must name it.

10) paper-vocab-and-wall — the premium block vocabulary with exact shapes (eyebrow/ingress/byline/stats/table/diagram/terminal/callout) from the showcase + optical payloads; the LIVE tag registry (exact-string); the publish-wall rules. Why: the flagship Paper is the deliverable; its block plan should be copy-ready at Decide.

11) boundary-census — everywhere Scaffy already lost, with evidence: D60 cuts (add-changeset, add-test-fixture, update-oban-cron, add-retriever, api-route-parity retired), deferred primitives (insert-before, value-capture, composition), D11's conditional/manual steps. Why: the boundary section of the Paper is mandatory under the honesty law.

12) authoring-cost — what it actually cost to author each .scaffy (W1/W5 slice task evidence: builder tokens, review rounds, line counts). Why: the crossover math needs the amortized numerator, not a guess.

13) validate-repo-ci — what validate --repo checks today (repocheck.go), its runtime, and the cheapest honest merge-gate integration (doc-gates.yml precedent, path triggers). Why: leap 3's build-cost estimate and whether it is a this-wave slice or a filed task.

14) novel-chore-control — find 2–3 real, recent one-off edits (from git log) that NO catalog command expresses, sized similar to the duel chores; recommend one as the boundary-control chore. Why: the control arm is what makes the benchmark falsifiable rather than a flatter-piece.

Ledger links

Epic: bp-scaffy-epic (charter .claude/workflows/bp-scaffy-charter.md, D1–D62 through W5). This Paper is the W6 living story: Digest appends the survey digest + verify plan; Decide appends the PRE-REGISTRATION (arms, chores, reps, thresholds — before any duel spends a token) + the wave plan with slice task ids; Review closes with the debrief and the flagship Paper link.

Survey digest — what 14 scouts established (Digest, 2026-07-17)

Ground truth of the tree. origin/main tip is 591fdcd53 (#3912 census heal). The local corpus is 12 .scaffy files, NOT 14 — add-schema-type + classify-block-type sit unmerged on the W5 round-2 branch (fc186b043, built, no PR, needs a rebase because its base predates #3912 and would silently revert the census). The SERVED catalog on guerrilla is still 7 (`bp scaffy ls --remote` live-verified) until W5 round 3 reseeds. PR #3917 is a byte-identical duplicate of merged #3912 — close it, never merge it. 591fdcd53 is RUN-PROVEN green for `CC=clang go test ./internal/scaffy/... ./internal/cli/...` in an isolated worktree — it is the duel pin SHA. The primary checkout is ~10 commits stale; every benchmark artifact reads origin/main or a pinned worktree, never this tree.

Methodology imported, then upgraded. The optical-duels prereg/results skeleton transfers cleanly: locked-predictions block, scoreboard table, symmetric observed-cons/observed-pros lists, and the closing adoption-doctrine table scoped ONLY to what was measured. W6 drops the 3-judge panel (our correctness axis is mechanical: repo gates). And W6 can be strictly MORE rigorous than its own precedent: both optical papers priced cost by chars/4 formula ('no metered API available'); we now have a real meter, live-proven twice over — `claude -p --output-format json` returns total_cost_usd, usage, num_turns, duration_ms per run, and session JSONL transcripts carry exact per-message API usage (which MUST be deduped by message.id or totals inflate 3.5-5x — 46 lines / 13 unique ids on the sampled file). Harness recipe verified: --model sonnet resolves to claude-sonnet-5; --max-budget-usd is the ONLY circuit breaker and hard-kills mid-task; a fresh session pays a ~$0.22 fixed context-load floor; --bare is unusable (OAuth-only sandbox); worktrees under /private/tmp are the proven isolation pattern.

Honesty-law findings the Paper must carry
(1) The W1 '56-80k tokens per hand-applied command' figure is UNSOURCED — two scouts independently exhausted every wave paper, all 7 W1 task evidence blobs, the charter, gh issue #3586, and repo-wide grep: the number exists only in this wave's own framing. It must be hedged as unmeasured or dropped; fresh arm-B numbers supersede it. (2) W5's frequency numbers (38 errors.ex clause-adds / 295 .ex+test co-creations / router.ex 739 partners) are agent hand-mined with no surviving script — commit counts reproduce (175 vs 173) but partner counts do NOT (naive filters give 968-1266, not 739); tooling/cochange.mjs did not produce them (it caps partners at 8). Cite as agent-produced, or re-mine with a documented pass. (3) Authoring cost has NO token record anywhere; the only honest proxy is review rounds — W1: 5 of 8 slices needed review fixes; W5 round 1: 6 of 6 clean. Authoring cost amortizes across the epic; never average W1 and W5 into one number.

Catalog census + cost-model corrections. All 12 commands censused with op counts and gate spines. Two corrections to the wave's own framing: add-block-type's JS gate leg measures 58s on a warm pnpm store (task-evidence, supersedes the 740s-cold charter figure — pin the environment model in prereg); and mechanical gate time across the ENTIRE lean matrix is ~7-8 minutes total — agent tokens dominate benchmark cost, gates are noise. A correctness-metric fork was discovered: 3 of 4 candidate chores carry TIER-ci Elixir gates the engine defers BY DESIGN (add-cli-verb, add-oban-worker, add-block-type's render_test leg), while add-error-shape's mix gate is LOCAL and measured 0.7s warm — prereg MUST pin whether 'gates green' means LOCAL-only (honest to a real dev session) or includes manually-invoked TIER-ci (true correctness), else vacuous green is baked into the benchmark. Chore-choice tension: strategy named add-cli-verb 'cheapest to repeat', but its gate is TIER-ci; ensure-cli-noun's gate is a pure-Go LOCAL test — the operationally cheapest in the catalog. Decide re-weighs the small-chore slot. Boundary-control chore picked from real history: the ExecRunner deadline fix (4adadf0e0, 2 files, report.go churned only 4x/6wk, no catalog command matches) — honest prediction: arm B wins or ties there.

Boundary + leaps groundwork done. The boundary section writes itself from evidence in hand: D60 cuts-with-evidence (add-changeset, add-test-fixture, update-oban-cron zero-instance, add-retriever below the >=3 bar, add-api-route-parity formally retired by w5-decide), D55 primitive verdicts (FOREACH rejected — its motivating legend is factually false; composition/insert-before/value-capture deferred with open backlog tasks), the D57 ensure-law (exit 4 = correct no-ownership outcome, reusing generic exitNotFound), and D11's still-manual judgment steps in the flagship itself (walk.ex kind dispatch). Leap 3 (CI drift gate): validate --repo is shipped and measured at 43-75ms on the real corpus, with ZERO CI wiring today; every concrete IN-target already rides doc-gates.yml's globs, the only missing trigger is scaffy/commands/** — a clean file-a-task, not on the duel critical path. Leap 2 (catalog-first doctrine) gets its measurement from the A vs A-prime arm gap.

Flagship Paper plumbing ready. Block shapes verified against compose.ex/data_viz.ex and the live optical papers: table `head` is canonical (header = legacy alias — pin ONE convention), stats items support max/spark/denom beyond label/value, diagram IS the mermaid block, terminal bodies are nested block children. Tag wall: all 90 live tags fetched — NONE of benchmark/duels/measurement exist; every new tag needs a published type:tag doc (_id = exact string) BEFORE the flagship publishes, or E3 422s. Reusable: scaffy (90-strength precedent), token-efficiency, research-note, docs, testing.

Coverage map — where scouts looked, and what was NOT found

Checked and found: W5 merge state (git+gh+ledger, live bp scaffy ls --remote), both optical papers block-by-block, JSONL token meter (live parse + dedup analysis), claude -p harness (two live probes incl. a budget-wall run), all 12 command files' ops+gates on origin/main, chore gate costs (task-evidence measured where it exists), charter D54-D62 verdict sheets, ensure-law code path (scaffy_cmd.go exit scheme + remove.go ReceiptMissingError), repocheck.go rules + live 43-75ms run, cochange.mjs read fully + live-run, tag registry mechanics + full live tag list, authoring-cost tables for all 16 slices, three candidate boundary chores with churn rates.

Checked and NOT found (absences are decisions-in-waiting): (a) No primary source for the 56-80k figure — anywhere. (b) No surviving script or filter definition behind the 38/295/739 mining numbers. (c) No CI workflow invokes bp scaffy validate in ANY form. (d) No token/turn record for authoring any .scaffy file. (e) No duel-harness script exists in the house — must be built. (f) No real chore-sized duel cell has ever been priced — the only measured number is a $0.22 no-op floor. Scaffy · Wave 6 · The Benchmark — measure it or don't ship it

Scaffy W6 — The Benchmark: duels, the use-case atlas, and the ascension leaps

WAVE COMPLETE (Review, 2026-07-17) — round 1 built and reviewed: 3 of 3 slices green (prereg paper published + tags registered; duel harness smoke-proven with review fixes; canonical miner deterministic). Rounds 2–3 (run-duels, flagship-paper) are DEFERRED BY DESIGN per D73 — dispatch after round 1 merges. Debrief at the bottom of this paper.

The wish

A large benchmarking test utilizing Scaffy to the max — documenting the usefulness of Scaffy and Barkpark, with a great flagship Paper as the deliverable. Real research: all use cases, potential leaps to ascend Scaffy into a token-sparing consistency speed machine, auto-detection of patterns, one clear understanding of what Scaffy IS. And the honesty law, in the user's own words: no bloat — we do not want to use it unless it actually performs A LOT better. A benchmark that only flatters is worthless.

This is W6 of the Scaffy epic: a MEASUREMENT wave. W1–W4 are sealed (7-command corpus, validate/fmt/run/remove/pull/ls --remote, commands served from guerrilla, reversibility matrix 6/6). W5 (catalog 7→14, ONEOF) is completing concurrently — rounds 2–3 in flight, PR #3917 healing the corpus count. W6 does not extend the catalog; it weighs it.

Direction (tentative — Decide finalizes after two exploration rounds)

The finished experience is TWO papers and a verdict. First, a short pre-registration paper (the optical-duels-prereg discipline: arms, chores, metrics, rep counts, and success thresholds committed BEFORE any duel runs — so the results cannot be quietly re-scoped to flatter). Second, THE flagship Paper: premium native blocks telling the whole story — one clear definition of what Scaffy is, the use-case atlas with frequency×pain evidence, the measured duel numbers, the honest boundary where Scaffy loses with a quantified crossover, and the leaps ranked with build-cost estimates. The verdict the Paper must be able to deliver honestly: 'use Scaffy for THESE shapes because it is measurably ~Nx cheaper/faster/more consistent; do NOT use it for THOSE, here is where the line sits.'

Duel design I lean toward (lean, pre-registered, small chores preferred for repetition): 3 catalog chores × 3 arms × up to 3 reps, plus one BOUNDARY CONTROL chore Scaffy should lose. Chores: add-error-shape (the frequency champion — 38 real clause-adds in errors.ex history), add-cli-verb (smallest, zero-Go, cheapest to repeat), add-oban-worker (REANCHOR accretion — run it TWICE per rep to measure the accretion case). Boundary control: a real, recent one-off edit no catalog command expresses — the arm-inversion that keeps the benchmark honest. The flagship add-block-type is the showpiece, not the workhorse: 1 rep, arm A vs arm C only (arm B at ~56–80k tokens × 3 surfaces × reps would blow the budget for a number W1 already gave us).

Arms: A = agent armed with bp scaffy run + the catalog, instructed catalog-first. B = bare agent hand-editing (the status quo). C = raw engine, no agent — zero tokens, milliseconds; C is nearly free so it runs for every chore and every rep and anchors the consistency floor (byte-determinism). A cheap A′ sub-duel where affordable: agent with scaffy AVAILABLE but NOT instructed catalog-first — this measures the doctrine gap, which is the real token-sparing machine (leap 2). Metrics per run, all mechanical: LLM tokens consumed, wall-clock, correctness (the repo's own gates green), consistency (byte-variance across reps — sha256 of the produced diff), reversibility (remove → git diff --stat empty). Every run in an isolated worktree pinned to one green base SHA (main's go suite may be red until #3917 merges — pin deliberately, never float).

Prior data folds in as evidence, cited not re-bought: W1's hand-apply pass burned ~56–80k tokens per command per agent doing what the engine does in milliseconds at zero tokens; W1's parallel builders shipped THREE grammar dialects in one wave (the consistency counterfactual); the 6/6 reversibility matrix (/papers/scaffy-reversibility-proof); W5's frequency mining (38 errors.ex clause-adds, 295 .ex+test co-creation commits, router.ex with 739 co-change partners). [Correction, 2026-07-17 Review: this direction paragraph predates the honesty sweep — D69 later ruled the 56–80k figure UNSOURCED (never citable as data), dropped 739 as irreproducible, and the pinned-window miner (tooling/scaffy-mine) superseded 295 with 236 strict / 304 loose co-creations. The sentence stands as the wave's starting belief, not as data.]

Leaps research (the ascension axis), each ending in a ranked verdict + build-cost estimate + filed task if ratified: (1) bp scaffy discover — spec the deterministic git-history mining pass (co-change accretion files, suffix-pair co-creations, directory fingerprints; W5 did this by hand agent-side — can it be a Go pass?), prototype if cheap; (2) agent-integration doctrine — how CLAUDE.md/skills should encode catalog-first so agents reach for the catalog instead of hand-editing (informed by the A vs A′ measurement); (3) CI/watch integration — anchors drift-checked on merge via validate --repo; (4) whatever the duels reveal. The crossover quantification is mandatory: authoring a .scaffy costs X once; it pays back at frequency × per-use savings — the atlas states, per use case, which side of the line it sits on.

Operational constraints binding this wave: W5 rounds 2–3 are completing concurrently — no build slice touches scaffy/commands/ or corpus_test.go until W5 round 3 merges (declare rounds/after honestly; the dispatcher consumes round/after natively). Duel agents are EXPENSIVE — the matrix is pre-registered BEFORE spending, and nothing outside the registered matrix runs. Benchmark runs happen in isolated worktrees, never the primary checkout (which is currently behind main and shows the 7-command corpus). New paper tags are pre-registered exact-string before publish.

Survey plan — 14 scouts, one question each

1) w5-live-state — exact merge state of W5 rounds 2–3 and PR #3917; is the served catalog 7 or 14; which files are hot; the last green base SHA to pin worktrees to. Why: the duel base and the do-not-touch set both depend on it.

2) duel-precedent — read /papers/optical-duels-prereg and /papers/optical-duels-results; extract the reusable methodology skeleton: what got pre-registered, how arms/judges/metrics were framed, what the results paper's block structure was. Why: W6 reuses that discipline wholesale.

3) token-accounting — the concrete mechanism to measure LLM tokens per duel run in this house (workflow harness stats, transcript files, claude CLI cost output?); where W1's 56–80k figure came from and whether the same instrument still exists. Why: tokens are the headline metric; without a trustworthy meter there is no benchmark.

4) w1-prior-evidence — dig up the primary records of the W1 hand-apply pass (task evidence, wave papers): exact token numbers per command, and the three-grammar-dialects story with cites. Why: prior data the Paper cites must be traceable to primary evidence, not memory.

5) catalog-census — every command in the current catalog (7 local, up to 14 on main): what it does, op census, gates, and a size/cost classification for duel-candidate sizing (which are small enough to repeat 3×). Why: chore selection wants the smallest chores that still represent each op family.

6) chore-gate-costs — for add-error-shape, add-cli-verb, add-oban-worker, add-block-type: the exact green gates and their measured local runtimes (mix test single-file ~2–9s warm, pnpm cold 740s, docs-anchors 70–154s…). Why: N reps × arms × gates is the wall-clock budget; the matrix must fit an afternoon.

7) frequency-evidence — where W5's mining numbers live (38 errors.ex clause-adds, 295 co-creation commits, router.ex 739 partners), the exact git commands used, and whether the pass is re-runnable/extendable. Why: the atlas's frequency column and the discover spec both stand on this method.

8) discover-prior-art — co-change mining prior art already in the repo: tooling/ (codebase-quality RELATE arc computes co-change layers), tooling/scope, any git-history analyzers. Why: bp scaffy discover should steal a proven pass, not invent one; build-cost estimate depends on what exists.

9) duel-harness — mechanics of running duel agents: how to spawn an isolated agent per arm (claude CLI? workflow?), model pinning (never Haiku; same model both arms), worktree setup/teardown, how to capture tokens+wall-clock+diff per run, cost estimate per duel cell. Why: the harness design gates everything; pre-registration must name it.

10) paper-vocab-and-wall — the premium block vocabulary with exact shapes (eyebrow/ingress/byline/stats/table/diagram/terminal/callout) from the showcase + optical payloads; the LIVE tag registry (exact-string); the publish-wall rules. Why: the flagship Paper is the deliverable; its block plan should be copy-ready at Decide.

11) boundary-census — everywhere Scaffy already lost, with evidence: D60 cuts (add-changeset, add-test-fixture, update-oban-cron, add-retriever, api-route-parity retired), deferred primitives (insert-before, value-capture, composition), D11's conditional/manual steps. Why: the boundary section of the Paper is mandatory under the honesty law.

12) authoring-cost — what it actually cost to author each .scaffy (W1/W5 slice task evidence: builder tokens, review rounds, line counts). Why: the crossover math needs the amortized numerator, not a guess.

13) validate-repo-ci — what validate --repo checks today (repocheck.go), its runtime, and the cheapest honest merge-gate integration (doc-gates.yml precedent, path triggers). Why: leap 3's build-cost estimate and whether it is a this-wave slice or a filed task.

14) novel-chore-control — find 2–3 real, recent one-off edits (from git log) that NO catalog command expresses, sized similar to the duel chores; recommend one as the boundary-control chore. Why: the control arm is what makes the benchmark falsifiable rather than a flatter-piece.

Ledger links

Epic: bp-scaffy-epic (charter .claude/workflows/bp-scaffy-charter.md, D1–D62 through W5). This Paper is the W6 living story: Digest appends the survey digest + verify plan; Decide appends the PRE-REGISTRATION (arms, chores, reps, thresholds — before any duel spends a token) + the wave plan with slice task ids; Review closes with the debrief and the flagship Paper link.

Survey digest — what 14 scouts established (Digest, 2026-07-17)

Ground truth of the tree. origin/main tip is 591fdcd53 (#3912 census heal). The local corpus is 12 .scaffy files, NOT 14 — add-schema-type + classify-block-type sit unmerged on the W5 round-2 branch (fc186b043, built, no PR, needs a rebase because its base predates #3912 and would silently revert the census). The SERVED catalog on guerrilla is still 7 (`bp scaffy ls --remote` live-verified) until W5 round 3 reseeds. PR #3917 is a byte-identical duplicate of merged #3912 — close it, never merge it. 591fdcd53 is RUN-PROVEN green for `CC=clang go test ./internal/scaffy/... ./internal/cli/...` in an isolated worktree — it is the duel pin SHA. The primary checkout is ~10 commits stale; every benchmark artifact reads origin/main or a pinned worktree, never this tree.

Methodology imported, then upgraded. The optical-duels prereg/results skeleton transfers cleanly: locked-predictions block, scoreboard table, symmetric observed-cons/observed-pros lists, and the closing adoption-doctrine table scoped ONLY to what was measured. W6 drops the 3-judge panel (our correctness axis is mechanical: repo gates). And W6 can be strictly MORE rigorous than its own precedent: both optical papers priced cost by chars/4 formula ('no metered API available'); we now have a real meter, live-proven twice over — `claude -p --output-format json` returns total_cost_usd, usage, num_turns, duration_ms per run, and session JSONL transcripts carry exact per-message API usage (which MUST be deduped by message.id or totals inflate 3.5-5x — 46 lines / 13 unique ids on the sampled file). Harness recipe verified: --model sonnet resolves to claude-sonnet-5; --max-budget-usd is the ONLY circuit breaker and hard-kills mid-task; a fresh session pays a ~$0.22 fixed context-load floor; --bare is unusable (OAuth-only sandbox); worktrees under /private/tmp are the proven isolation pattern.

Honesty-law findings the Paper must carry (1) The W1 '56-80k tokens per hand-applied command' figure is UNSOURCED — two scouts independently exhausted every wave paper, all 7 W1 task evidence blobs, the charter, gh issue #3586, and repo-wide grep: the number exists only in this wave's own framing. It must be hedged as unmeasured or dropped; fresh arm-B numbers supersede it. (2) W5's frequency numbers (38 errors.ex clause-adds / 295 .ex+test co-creations / router.ex 739 partners) are agent hand-mined with no surviving script — commit counts reproduce (175 vs 173) but partner counts do NOT (naive filters give 968-1266, not 739); tooling/cochange.mjs did not produce them (it caps partners at 8). Cite as agent-produced, or re-mine with a documented pass. (3) Authoring cost has NO token record anywhere; the only honest proxy is review rounds — W1: 5 of 8 slices needed review fixes; W5 round 1: 6 of 6 clean. Authoring cost amortizes across the epic; never average W1 and W5 into one number.

Catalog census + cost-model corrections. All 12 commands censused with op counts and gate spines. Two corrections to the wave's own framing: add-block-type's JS gate leg measures 58s on a warm pnpm store (task-evidence, supersedes the 740s-cold charter figure — pin the environment model in prereg); and mechanical gate time across the ENTIRE lean matrix is ~7-8 minutes total — agent tokens dominate benchmark cost, gates are noise. Chore-choice tension: strategy named add-cli-verb 'cheapest to repeat', but its gate is TIER-ci; ensure-cli-noun's gate is a pure-Go LOCAL test — the operationally cheapest in the catalog.
